subject: Demo recap + POC plan for FinServCorp
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: James Liu <james.liu@finservcorp.com>; Priya Singh <priya.singh@finservcorp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Demo recap + POC plan for FinServCorp

Thanks again for your time today — really appreciate the thoughtful questions. Quick recap from our demo and a proposed 3-week POC to validate performance and integration for your document ingestion + retrieval use case.

Summary of demo
- Walkthrough: Redwood hosted inference, dedicated routing, and prefix caching for latency-sensitive retrieval responses.
- Highlight: Streaming responses + SDK integrations and cost controls (batching/quantization).

Proposed POC objective
- Goal: Demonstrate sub-150ms median latency for 1-2k qps simulation on representative documents and validate end-to-end retrieval accuracy for 5 core intents.

Success criteria (what FinServCorp will validate)
1) Latency: median token response < 150ms under test load (70th percentile < 220ms)
2) Throughput: sustained 1k qps with error rate < 1%
3) Quality: end-to-end retrieval precision >= 85% on agreed eval set
4) Security: SOC2-compliant logging + S3 encryption in transit at rest; confirm IAM roles and access pattern

POC plan (high level)
- Week 0 (prep): exchange sample data, enable VPC peering / S3 access, scope ACLs (owner: Priya, Redwood owner: Marissa)
- Week 1 (integration): ingest sample set, baseline runs, collect traces (owner: Dev)
- Week 2 (scale + tune): load tests, batching/quantization experiments, latency tuning (owner: Dev + Marissa)
- Week 3 (evaluation + wrap): run eval set, joint review, next steps/contract (owner: Marissa + FinServ PDL)

Deliverables
- POC runbook and checklist (attached: FinServ_POC_Plan_v1.pdf)
- Temporary dedicated capacity estimate and cost window
- SOW draft for execution (attached: SOW_draft_finserv_2026.docx)

Immediate next steps
1) Can you confirm the sample dataset location (S3 prefix) and point of contact for infra access?
2) Are the success criteria above aligned with your expectations or should we adjust thresholds?
3) Preferred kickoff date — we proposed week of Mar 22; Mar 24 works for us for a 30-min technical kickoff.

If that all looks good I'll send a formal calendar invite and loop in our solutions engineer (Dev) and CS lead (Rachel) for kickoff.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

--

Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap + POC plan for FinServCorp

Thanks Marissa — quick tech clarifications so I can size infra and prepare test harness:
- For the eval set, what is the avg doc size and token distribution? (rough tokens per document)
- Do they expect encrypted at rest S3 only or also a VPC endpoint with restricted egress?
- Any PII masking required before we ingest?

Also, can we confirm whether FinServCorp prefers hosted Redwood Dedicated for the POC or a short-lived Private deployment? Dedicated is faster to stand up; Private will need additional network setup.

Planning to prepare a replayable load test (locust) and a small evaluation harness for precision metrics. Will share the checklist by EOD Monday.

- Dev
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwoodinference.com

From: James Liu <james.liu@finservcorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@finservcorp.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo recap + POC plan for FinServCorp

Marissa — thanks for the clear plan. High level answers:
- Sample dataset: ~12k documents, avg ~450 tokens (range 80-2.5k). I can share an S3 prefix with read-only service account. (owner: Priya)
- Security: We need TLS + server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) and access via VPC endpoint. SOC2 evidence is required before going live; for POC it's fine to use scoped service account + audit logs.
- Success criteria: latency and throughput targets look reasonable; for quality we'll initially accept >= 80% precision, but would like to track recall as well.

We’re aligned on the Mar 24 kickoff — morning PST preferred. Can you send a 30-min invite? Also please share the eval set schema and the runbook.

Thanks,
James
Principal Product Manager | FinServCorp
james.liu@finservcorp.com

I’ll circulate the calendar invite and the Drive link to the runbook by EOD. Looking forward to getting started.

Marissa
